title: PH extends 14-day visa-free entry for Chinese nationals until January 2028 -- DFA
summary: The 14-day visa-free entry privilege for Chinese nationals has been extended until January 15, 2028, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) announced Sunday.

blocks.text: The 14-day visa-free entry privilege for Chinese nationals has been extended until January 15, 2028, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) announced Sunday.

In a press release, the DFA said the extension aligns with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s directive to “boost international tourist arrivals and investment in the Philippines, while maintaining existing immigration and national security safeguards.”
The visa-free privilege applies only to Chinese nationals visiting strictly for tourism or business and staying up to 14 days.
To qualify, travelers must hold a passport valid for at least six months beyond their intended stay, along with confirmed hotel accommodations and a return or onward ticket.
The privilege remains non-extendable and non-convertible to any other Philippine visa category.

“The extension remains subject to existing immigration and security safeguards, including the allowed entry of Chinese nationals availing of the visa-free entry privilege through the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) in Metro Manila and Mactan-Cebu International Airport (MCIA) in Cebu only. Travelers must comply with applicable eTravel registration requirements and have no derogatory records with the Bureau of Immigration (BI),” the DFA said.

“Further, admission into the Philippines remains subject to inspection, screening procedures, and determination by the BI, including applicable identity verification, watchlist checks, and risk-based assessment,” it added.
The agency emphasized that throughout the implementation of the 14-day visa-free policy, it will maintain close coordination with the BI.
DFA reminded Chinese travelers transiting through the Philippines en route to a third destination that they must secure the appropriate Philippine transit visa before entry.—LDF, GMA News
